title: Advice on making a clarinet part and jazzing tunes
summary: Picou says they changed waltz time to jazz time and figured out clarinet parts by ear while the band played.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well, if you were talking to a young fellow now that was getting ready to be a professional musician, is there any special advice that you would give him?
What would you tell him? What would you tell Ralph here about?

How you blow it, that's all. The right way to blow it. In other words, to learn his horn. Yes, that's the first one. What I would like to do with some of this material that you are recording, I would like to, if possible, get some of it published someday. If you had any advice to give about playing like in a jazz band, just what you do with a tune, so that young musicians that are coming up and will come up in future years would have an idea just what your advice would be. If you are going to play any kind of a late popular tune, just any kind of a tune, what do you try to do when you make up your clarinet part? Well, I'll tell you how we used to do it. We had our band and they asked us to play a waltz. All right. We played that waltz in a waltz time. And then we change it to jazz time. That's it. Jazz time. When you play it in jazz time, do you try to play more notes or what do you do to change the melody? How do you change it? How do you change it? Aside from changing the time, I know you change the time. Well, it's to change the time, that's all. Otherwise you...

As a clarinet player, do you find that you yourself prefer to play more melody or harmony? That is, do you leave the melody to the trumpet player and play the clarinet harmony part or do you have a tendency to sometimes want to play the melody itself in the ensemble?

I've wondered about the variations that you make if you try to just play a lot of chords, or if you'd rather play sort of a counter melody sometime, what do you think sounds best on the clarinet? Well, that depends what they got in you about variations.
Do you usually find that you like to practice your clarinet part or do you like to wait until the band is playing and then figure it out while they're playing?
It always comes out better that way. Yes, it comes right to you. You don't try to memorize things. No, no. It all comes to you.
